voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, Jack - Deep Dark Horror Narrator (BVPhWQykET1TSvfGzrUr), English, one take, split into lines, inner pauses capped at 0.32 s, atempo 1.0

lines.text: The most famous ghost photograph ever taken. Watch it develop.
lines.beat_before: hook: the darkroom, red light; a print in the tray; the image surfacing: a staircase, a pale shape

lines.text: Raynham Hall, Norfolk. September, nineteen thirty-six. Two photographers from Country Life magazine.
lines.beat_before: cut to the house at night; a motor car comes up the drive, its headlights across the front

lines.text: They had taken one picture of the great staircase. They were setting up a second.
lines.beat_before: cut to the hall: the view camera on its tripod; the first flash goes off; nothing on the stairs

lines.text: Then the assistant saw something on the stairs. A shape, like vapour, coming down towards them. Slowly becoming a woman.
lines.beat_before: cut to the ground glass under the focusing cloth: the stairs, upside down; a pale shape at the top

lines.text: He shouted, take it. The flash went off. The other man saw nothing.
lines.beat_before: on the ground glass the shape comes down; cut to the hall in the dark

lines.text: Country Life printed it that December. Experts said the negative had not been touched.
lines.beat_before: the flash: she is on the stairs; then the lamp: the stairs are empty; the darkroom

lines.text: Skeptics say double exposure. Or something on the lens.
lines.beat_before: the print developing: she comes up out of the paper

lines.text: People had reported a lady in brown on these stairs for a hundred years.
lines.beat_before: the staircase by moonlight, climbing; a figure on the landing against the window, then not
the darkroom: the print in the stop bath
